title: Restore the input group for Voxtype evdev hotkey users
head: d1943054f14c
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A failed user/group lookup is interpreted as absence, then grants raw input access
leads.consequence: With voxtype reporting true, an error from id (for example an invalid or stale $USER/NSS lookup) makes grep find no input and the negated pipeline succeed, even under pipefail. The script calls sudo gpasswd -a $USER input rather than stopping; depending on whether that account exists, it either fails and leaves migration pending or grants the wrong account input access. The fixture id stub always succeeds, so it cannot catch this. Distinguish an unsuccessful id from a successful absence.
leads.triage: dropped; id -nG fails only for an unresolvable account; gpasswd -a on the same name then fails and the migration stops for retry. Stub run does not reflect real gpasswd; no wrong-account grant.

leads.summary: Migration uses an environment-supplied account name for the privileged group grant
leads.consequence: The migration runs for the current user but reads $USER rather than the real current account: a shell/hook that exports another valid username causes id to check that account and sudo gpasswd to grant it input instead, leaving the migrating user's evdev key inaccessible while the other account gains unrestricted keyboard-event access. If id on that account fails, H1 applies. Resolve identity with id -un, then check that account's groups. Related open #8534 fixes precisely this environment-variable issue in other privileged Omarchy commands but not this new migration.

leads.summary: Revoking the Voxtype opt-in does not revoke its input grant
leads.consequence: After this migration adds a user to input solely for Voxtype, disabling the evdev hotkey or choosing Remove > AI > Dictation leaves the account in input indefinitely, even after a logout or reboot. Any user process still has access to the keyboard's event device although the only reason for granting it has gone. The remover deletes the package and config but never checks/revokes group membership; avoid blindly removing membership if xpadneo/ydotool or an independent user choice still requires it, for example track ownership of this grant and verify other users of it.
leads.triage: dropped; same lifecycle as existing xpadneo/ydotool exceptions; out of PR scope

leads.summary: Turning on the hotkey after this one-time migration leaves it without input access
leads.consequence: The default installed config explicitly sets enabled=false, so the one-time migration finishes and is marked done for that account. If the user later enables built-in evdev via voxtype configure or installs and enables Voxtype after upgrading, neither the installer nor the TUI adds input membership and omarchy-migrate will skip its marker forever. The evdev hotkey remains broken with no explanation. New users inherit the migration marker from /etc/skel. Provide an explicit opt-in setup path (plus user guidance in manual/11-text-extraction-dictation.md:13-15) outside a one-shot migration.
leads.triage: dropped; inherent to one-shot migrations; voxtype setup check names the fix; covered in spirit by design point

leads.summary: An unavailable or unsupported Voxtype config getter is permanently treated as disabled
leads.consequence: If voxtype is on PATH but config get hotkey.enabled exits unsuccessfully with empty output (for example older Voxtype v0.7.5, which has config set but no config get, or a temporarily unreadable/malformed config), the comparison is false, the migration succeeds, and the runner creates its completion marker. Repairing or upgrading the binary/config later will never retry the missing group grant. Treat a failed getter as a failed migration or use a supported source with an explicit error path, rather than suppressing all errors and completing it.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F6/F1; published as Note and F1

leads.summary: The getter's effective value is not necessarily what the running daemon uses
leads.consequence: The 1.0.1 getter resolves the launching process's file, defaults and environment, not the already-running daemon or its systemd-specific overrides. A user service drop-in with Environment=VOXTYPE_HOTKEY_ENABLED=true and the stock file enabled=false produces false in the migration and misses a needed grant; a drop-in with false and file enabled=true produces a grant even though the daemon's evdev listener is off. A daemon ExecStart with --config or --no-hotkey similarly diverges. The systemd unit and optional user overrides should be accounted for before treating CLI output as daemon opt-in.

leads.summary: Missing user config silently broadens an opt-in group grant
leads.consequence: If Voxtype is present but the user's config file was removed or not provisioned, v1.0.1 config get returns the built-in default true; the migration grants access to all raw input devices without anyone explicitly choosing enabled=true, contrary to the comment's opt-in-only security rationale. The stock installer copies enabled=false but is not the only way a binary can be present, and a deleted/empty config re-enables the upstream listener. If requiring opt-in is intentional, inspect file_value via --json (taking into account the daemon's environment) or require explicit user confirmation.
leads.triage: dropped; bin/omarchy-voxtype-install:14-15 always copies default config (enabled=false); without a config the daemon's hotkey is active so the grant matches daemon behaviour

leads.summary: The group lookup matches other valid group names that contain input
leads.consequence: grep -w input treats a hyphen as a non-word delimiter. A user who belongs to a different group named input-alt is incorrectly considered already in input, receives neither gpasswd nor reboot-required, and migration is marked complete, leaving the evdev hotkey broken. Tokenize id -nG on spaces and compare entire group names with grep -x (as bin/omarchy-dev-install-ydoo:15 does). Add a fixture for 'wheel input-alt'.
leads.triage: dropped; true but needs a nonexistent group name; same pattern as 1787865477; nitpick

leads.summary: Voxtype's default logging writes configuration warnings to the getter's stdout, defeating an exact true comparison
leads.consequence: At v1.0.1, an unrelated invalid but nonfatal environment override such as VOXTYPE_ENGINE=bogus logs 'Unknown VOXTYPE_ENGINE value: bogus' before config get hotkey.enabled prints true. The standard tracing subscriber writes those warnings to stdout. The command substitution therefore includes a warning line as well as true, fails equality, and the runner marks this migration completed while the daemon may still have its evdev hotkey enabled. Redirecting stderr does not help; consume structured output with an appropriate quiet/logging mode and handle errors separately.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1 mechanism (additional trigger, Sol-only evidence); not named publicly, fix covers it

leads.summary: Related #12895 invalidates the new migration comment's controller-grant premise
leads.consequence: Open #12895 removes input-group membership from the Xbox-controller installer because joystick uaccess already suffices. If both PRs merge, this new comment still says that the controller installer grants input as an opt-in feature needing it, although it does not. The unchanged older migration still preserves old xpadneo memberships; this is a stale security rationale, not a merge conflict or a functional regression of Voxtype. Adjust the comment if #12895 lands first.
leads.triage: dropped; comment describes 1787865477, which stays accurate; not a conflict

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new migration restores `input` for users who opted into Voxtype's evdev hotkey and leaves Omarchy's default compositor-bound setup alone, for both already-affected machines and late updaters who run 1787865477 and 1789490499 in the same update. Gating on `voxtype config get hotkey.enabled` rather than grepping the TOML is the right source: a `[hotkey]` section without `enabled` resolves to Voxtype's built-in default `true`, which matches what the daemon does. One robustness gap remains with the Voxtype version Omarchy currently packages (1.1.0), plus a hardening point on the target account.

Real `omarchy-migrate` with stubbed group, sudo, pacman and state commands and real Voxtype 1.0.1 and 1.1.0 binaries:

| Scenario | End groups | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Late updater, hotkey on | `wheel input` | `-d` from 1787865477, then `-a` from 1789490499 |
| Late updater, Omarchy default config | `wheel` | removed, not restored |
| Late updater, ydotool installed, hotkey on | `wheel input` | kept, no churn |
| Already affected, hotkey on | `wheel input` | restored |
| Already affected, default config | `wheel` | untouched |
| Voxtype not installed / already in `input` | unchanged | untouched |

### Log lines on stdout can defeat the `== "true"` check

Voxtype sends its tracing output to stdout, and the condition compares the whole captured stdout with `true`:

```bash
[[ $(voxtype config get hotkey.enabled 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]
```

Two cases put log lines in front of `true`:

- **Voxtype 1.1.0, hotkey on, one config section it cannot read** (for example `max_duration_secs = "sixty"` in `[audio]`): 1.1.0 skips that section with two `WARN` lines on stdout, exits 0 and still resolves `hotkey.enabled` to `true`.
- **`RUST_LOG` set to `debug` or `trace` in the update's environment** (1.0.1 and 1.1.0): a `DEBUG Loading config from ...` line is printed first.

```text
stdout (1.1.0, bad [audio] value, hotkey on):
  WARN Config section 'audio' could not be read and is using defaults. ...
  WARN 1 config section(s) were skipped: audio
  true
condition: false  ->  no gpasswd call, migration marked complete
```

**Impact:** in these cases the migration records itself as done without restoring the group. With 1.1.0 the daemon keeps running on the salvaged config with the hotkey enabled (per Voxtype's source), so the user stays in the broken state this PR fixes, and the migration never runs again. This needs the hotkey opt-in plus one of the two conditions above, so it is an edge case.

**Suggested change:** silence tracing for the query:

```bash
[[ $(RUST_LOG=off voxtype config get hotkey.enabled 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]
```

With this change, both cases above restore the group, and every other scenario in the table keeps the same outcome. `voxtype -q` covers the `WARN` case but not `RUST_LOG=debug`, because the environment filter takes precedence over `-q`. The PR's test stub still matches the arguments.

### Group target comes from `$USER`

`id -nG "$USER"` and `sudo gpasswd -a "$USER" input` take the account name from the environment. A different `USER` value makes the sudo-backed grant add `input` to another account. Open PR #8534 ("Take privileged usernames from id -un, not USER") makes the same argument for sibling privileged commands but does not cover a new migration. 1787865477 uses the same pattern, but for a removal rather than a grant.

**Impact:** the privileged grant's target is not tied to the account running the update.

**Suggested change:** resolve the account once with `user=$(id -un)` and use it in both calls. The test's `id` stub would then also need to answer `-un`.

### Design point: the grant is gated on user-writable state

For maintainers to weigh. 1787865477 keeps `input` only on root-owned package state (`pacman -Qq xpadneo-dkms` or `ydotool`). This migration grants `input` through sudo based on `~/.config/voxtype/config.toml`, or on `VOXTYPE_HOTKEY_ENABLED=1` (or `true`) if that is set in the update's environment (it yields `true` even with Omarchy's default config). Any process running as the user can set either before the next update. It is also a first-time grant for users who never had the group (installs made from 4.0.2 until this migration ships, where the hotkey was enabled in the meantime). **Impact:** a sudo-backed `input` grant can be triggered by user-writable config or environment state. The window is a single migration run and requires an existing same-user compromise, and the opt-in does reflect user intent.

**Optional approaches:** keep the automatic grant as is, or notify affected users and print the one command instead of granting automatically.

**Optional test improvement:** the added test kills five of six diagnostic mutants of the migration, but not a fail-open comparison (`!= "false"` in place of `== "true"`), which grants `input` whenever `voxtype config get` fails or prints nothing. A fifth case with a `voxtype` stub that exits non-zero with empty stdout, asserting no `gpasswd` call, separates the two (original: no grant; mutant: grant).

**Comment accuracy:** migrations/1789490499.sh lines 13-14 say a bare modifier "cannot be bound in Hyprland at all". #7302 reports that press binds on a lone modifier fire and only the release bind never fires (hyprwm/Hyprland#6946), so hold-to-talk is what is impossible. Suggested wording: "push-to-talk on a bare modifier can't be done with Hyprland binds (hyprwm/Hyprland#6946)".

**Note:** Voxtype before 1.0.0 has no `config get` (0.7.5 exits 2 with "unrecognized subcommand"), so the migration skips silently and marks itself done. This is unlikely in practice, because `omarchy update` upgrades packages before running migrations and Omarchy's voxtype-bin PKGBUILD moved to 1.0.0 on 2026-09-01.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head d1943054 against base 2fbac0c8 and Voxtype source at v0.7.5, v1.0.1 and v1.1.0. The PR test, six diagnostic mutants and real `omarchy-migrate` ran in an isolated sandbox with released Voxtype 0.7.5, 1.0.1 and 1.1.0 binaries and stubbed `id`, `sudo`, `gpasswd`, `pacman` and `omarchy-state`. No real group, sudo or account changes were made, and the hotkey itself was not exercised on a live session.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
